subject: Planned maintenance: North-USEast (us-east-3) rolling refresh — 2026-09-22 02:00-08:00 UTC
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: support@acme-retail.com, ops@acme-retail.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Planned maintenance: North-USEast (us-east-3) rolling refresh — 2026-09-22 02:00-08:00 UTC

Hi Ben / Acme ops team,

Quick heads-up from Redwood Infra: we have a planned, rolling infrastructure refresh for the us-east-3 inference cluster on 2026-09-22 between 02:00 and 08:00 UTC. This is a region-scoped, staggered restart to apply a new kernel micro-patch plus updated NVIDIA driver bits that address a recent CVE mitigation and provide improved kernel scheduling (expected CPU/GPU tail-latency improvements).

What to expect
- Window: 2026-09-22 02:00 — 08:00 UTC (staggered across racks).
- Impact per node: ephemeral service interruption during restart (~20–45 seconds for a node rebind).
- Behavioral notes: streaming generations may observe a short reconnect/stream gap; in-progress short-running requests should complete on alternate warm nodes; long-running KV-warmed sessions may need a warm-up pass post-maintenance.
- Duration: We expect the full region rollout to complete within the 6-hour window; any outliers will be communicated.
- SLA: This is a scheduled maintenance event. If you have an extenuating blackout window, please reply by EOD 2026-09-16.

Recommended actions for Acme (optional)
- Pause non-urgent large-batch embedding jobs during the window.
- For critical low-latency routes, enable client-side retries with idempotency tokens and a 10s retry delay to avoid bursts during node restarts.
- If you use dedicated clusters: let us know if you want this maintenance deferred to a customer blackout window (per your dedicated contract).

Attachments: northus_rolling_refresh_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 280 KB), kernel-micropatch-notes.txt (TXT, 3 KB)

We’ll post live status updates to the region incident page during the window and will send a post-maintenance summary once the rollout completes.

If you’d like a 30-minute pre-window sync between our SREs and your ops team, we can schedule that.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Lead — Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Hi Ben — thanks for the fast reply. Short answers:

1) Dedicated clusters: we do not include customer-provisioned Dedicated VMs in the standard shared-hosted rollout by default. However, for Dedicated environments that are managed by Redwood (your DC1 tenancy), we can either schedule the same patch window (recommended for parity) or defer to a customer blackout window. Please confirm if DC1 is managed by Redwood or customer-self-managed.

2) Runtime behavior: the patch is kernel/driver-level and does not change model weights or the runtime API contract. Streaming sessions may see short reconnects during node restarts (20–45s) but will resume; we recommend keeping client-side reconnect logic enabled. For long-running sessions we can coordinate a pre-roll warm-up after the window to rehydrate caches.

3) SLA / credits: scheduled maintenance is excluded from standard downtime SLA credit calculations. For enterprise accounts, we can make exceptions on a case-by-case basis. If you require a contractual credit/one-off concession, please flag that and we’ll triage with finance & account execs.

Estimated first-impact: we plan to start node restarts at ~02:15 UTC (after final validations) and will proceed in small batches with ~5–10 minute spacing between rack groups. We’ll publish per-rack progress updates to the shared doc listed below.

If you prefer a blackout, reply with preferred window by EOD 2026-09-16; otherwise we’ll proceed with the planned window. Would it help to do a 30-min ops sync on 2026-09-21 23:30 UTC?

Attachments referenced: northus_rolling_refresh_plan_v1.pdf

Best,
Monica Patel

Redwood Inference

Monica / Jordan — quick internal note to land next steps before Ben hears back:

Per our standard, scheduled maintenance is excluded but for ACME (enterprise/high-value) we should consider a one-off concession if they have an active dedicated tenancy we manage. Recommend: offer a 1% service credit if they insist on a deferred maintenance + commit to a preferred blackout date (our ops can run a special maintenance then).

- Jordan: if we offer the defer + 1% credit, can infra run the specialized deferred-window on 2026-10-06 02:00-06:00 UTC? If yes, reply-all and I’ll propose that to Ben.

- Action: draft a short amendment for finance approval (I’ll open HS-78654) and loop in legal if they want contract language.

Minutes: schedule a quick 15-min call if you need to align — proposing 2026-09-16 17:00 UTC.
